facts.text: Grip is a Bullet3-powered prototyping toolbox for manipulation environments, robot arms, grippers and RGBD cameras, with ROS2 integration
The Env abstract base declares step(action), reset() and render(mode)
TemplateEnvironment is defined as an Env subclass
PickAndPlaceEnvironment is defined as a TemplateEnvironment subclass
The constructor reads seed (default 77) and seeds Python's random and NumPy's generator with it
The constructor defaults time_step to 1/240 s and sim_steps to 10
The constructor creates a BulletWorld with the configured render mode, real_time_sim False and the time step
The environment spawns a BulletPandaArmGripper with the configured gripper type and maximum force
init registers the plane, robot and table, the shoulder camera for the selected modes and the wrist camera for the wrist/all modes
reset restores the world state, resets the panda and returns obs()
step applies joint_position_cmd with set_angles and gripper_cmd with control_fingers or apply_gripper_delta_action, advances sim_steps world steps and returns (obs, reward, done, info)
obs returns each entity's state and, unless camera_mode is none, each camera's rgb, depth, seg and pose
sample returns seven joint-position values and one gripper value drawn with np.random.randn
PickAndPlaceEnvironment adds a fixed tray and a free duck object loaded from pybullet_data URDFs
The panda arm controls panda_joint1 through panda_joint7 and defaults gripper_max_force to 12
PandaGripper.apply_gripper_delta_action takes a delta finger-distance action, adds it to the finger positions and clips each finger to its lower and upper joint limit
The documented pure-python example runs the pick-and-place environment with python3 -m grip_examples.environments.ex01_pick_and_place
The runtime dependencies include NumPy, pybullet, open3d, OpenCV and Matplotlib

determinism.notes: the upstream constructor seeds Python and NumPy once (template_env.py:34-37) and reset() has no seed argument, so this driver exposes no seed control; the fake is deterministic for a fixed action sequence but claims no seeded-replay contract and was not compared with upstream

gaps: the fake is a pure-Python kinematic stand-in: no pybullet, rigid-body dynamics, contacts, friction, gripper contact, camera rendering or point-cloud pipeline

one cap.world.step.v1 tick models the upstream constructor defaults of 10 world steps of 1/240 s (template_env.py:42-43); both are configurable per environment instance and the fake uses fixed placeholder values

the observation is a reduced JSON object with robot joint positions/velocities/efforts and object and tray poses; the upstream observation also carries entity pointers, plane/table states and camera rgb, depth and segmentation arrays (template_env.py:190-204), which are omitted

the fake accepts a numeric gripper delta finger-distance command only; the upstream step also accepts the strings 'open' and 'close' (template_env.py:170-174), which the published schema does not expose

reset performs no seeding: the upstream reset takes no seed argument and the environment seeds its generators only in the constructor; the reset receipt reports the selected constructor seed, without claiming reset reseeding
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state/set_state pair
the real pybullet environment needs pybullet, NumPy, open3d, OpenCV and Matplotlib (pyproject.toml:10-24); nothing was installed or run where the gate ran
no physical device is modelled and nothing was validated against one
